title: Meteor shower seen at Fort Wayne's Night of Lights continues
excerpt: A roundup of news for Fort Wayne, Allen County and surrounding areas.
content:
Fort Wayne/Allen County

Meteor shower seen locally continues

A meteor shower that produced a fireball seen by visitors at an annual downtown Fort Wayne celebration is expected to last until Dec. 10.

The green fireball appeared in the middle of a drone show at the Night of Lights on Wednesday. Lightings at several downtown locations preceded the drone show.

City Clerk John McGauley captured the meteor’s passing in a video of the drone show. It was shared by many Facebook accounts, including the city of Fort Wayne’s.

“A meteor made an unexpected appearance over downtown Fort Wayne tonight,” the city’s post said.

The Northern Taurids meteor shower began Oct. 20 and is expected to last into December, according to the American Meteor Society website. The peak night was Nov. 11.

The organization expected reduced visibility this week that could affect the ability to see such fireballs because the moon reached its full phase Tuesday, illuminating the sky, according to an activity outlook posted Monday.

The video had been viewed about 219,000 times as of Friday morning, McGauley said in a Facebook post. It has been picked up on national news networks and media outlets.

PFW, IUFW seeking donations

Two local university campuses are seeking donations to its annual program that helps students facing financial need provide holiday gifts for their families.

Students at Purdue University Fort Wayne and Indiana University Fort Wayne can apply to participate in the program. Faculty, staff, departments and students organizations sign up to sponsor families and shop for items, a news release said.

“We know our students are balancing school with responsibilities at home, and the holidays can bring extra expenses for their families,”

Monetary donations from the community help support the program, the release said.

Giang Petroviak, PFW executive director of student success initiatives, said in a statement. “Something as simple as warm clothing or a gift for a child can make a difference for a student who’s trying to make the holidays special for their family.”

Donations can be dropped off at the Office of Student Success Initiatives in Walb Student Union, Room 118, by Tuesday.

– The Journal Gazette
